result.title: Feeling of Knowing in Large Language Models
result.summary: Post-training updates change what large language models (LLMs) can answer, but may leave their answerability judgments misaligned. We study this knowledge-judgment desynchronization through functional feeling of knowing (FoK), which supports selective generation, retrieval triggering, and model routing without implying subjective experience. We propose two trainable channels: a knowledge channel that changes answerability and a FoK channel that judges the current knowledge state. Three stages train them: on-policy supervised fine-tuning (OP-SFT) updates knowledge from corrected on-policy answers; knowledge-delta FoK training (K$Δ$-FT) adapts judgments across intermediate knowledge states; and FoK-guided policy optimization (FGPO) trains the subsequent answer or explanation. Factual-QA experiments, cross-dataset evaluation, and three sequential updates show that explicit FoK alignment improves judgment quality on updated knowledge. MMLU and ARC-Easy separately assess capability preservation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出功能性「感 knowledge」（FoK）框架，把知识更新与可答性判断拆为两条可训练通道，并用三阶段训练（OP-SFT、知识差量 FoK 训练、FoK 引导策略优化）让判断跟上中间知识状态。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「知识通道／判断通道」解耦与跨中间状态的监督，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态内容与「何时作答、何时检索或停止」判定的分离训练提供借鉴线索，是否适用于多模态推理期状态尚待核查。
